methodology_note: The review's grading model and its reading of the verified scorer are accurate: I confirmed every fact against the snapshot and the working-repo scorer, and every replay-based claim I re-ran (about 40 alternative trajectories) reproduced. Substantive findings are sound for all 20 tasks, and I found no fabricated or misquoted citations. The main weakness is severity calibration across reviewers rather than evidence: the same defect classes (criterion-4 provisional credit, presence-only ACTION grading, unscripted expedited shipping, cosmetic doc corruption) received different severities in different tasks, and I adjusted five tasks (034, 038, 039, 040, 044) to the calibration file. Blind spots: the review generally does not consider post-retention follow-ups the simulator might trigger (e.g. the customer still asking to close the original card after applying for the recommended one in 044/047/048; the gold assumes 'apply instead of closing'), and it missed the task_046 seed dispute whose last-4 matches neither of the customer's cards. Several verdicts depend on the verified relaxations, and each review file says so: the closure_reason strip neutralizes the Crypto reason ambiguity in 048, and the subset rule tolerates the failed payment attempt in 049. Neither changes a severity here.
